turns.text: 10:31 am question. when do babies usually outgrow size 1 diapers? theo is 7 weeks (born july 19) and i'm trying to figure out when to reorder. please and thanks

Most brands list size 1 for roughly 8-14 lbs, so many babies move up to size 2 somewhere between 2 and 4 months. Weight matters more than age. Signs it's time: red marks on the thighs or waist, leaks or blowouts that were rare before, tabs that barely reach the center, or the diaper looking stretched and low. If you tell me his current weight I can estimate how close he is.
last weigh in was 12 lb 3 oz at his 2 month. so basically at the top of the range? can you put sizing in table form, i think better in tables

Here's the typical range (it varies a bit by brand, so check the package):

| Size | Typical weight | Typical age |
|---|---|---|
| Newborn | up to 10 lb | first few weeks |
| 1 | 8-14 lb | ~2-4 months |
| 2 | 12-18 lb | ~3-8 months |
| 3 | 16-28 lb | ~5-12+ months |

The overlap is intentional: at 12 lb 3 oz he fits both 1 and 2. If he's not leaking, you can finish size 1, but I'd buy size 2 for the next order rather than another big size 1 box.

ok that helps. so here's the thing, we don't do delivery for groceries anymore, i go to ruiz family market saturdays with him in the carrier. delivery is only for diapers now so i have to order ahead and not run out. also we started the gentle formula this week, could that change diaper output? 🙃

Yes, it can. Switching formulas often changes stool color, consistency and frequency for a week or two. Partially hydrolyzed formulas tend to produce softer or slightly greener stools, and wet diapers should stay about the same. That means a bit more diaper use is possible during the transition, so it's worth keeping a small buffer. Call the pediatrician if you see very few wet diapers, blood or mucus in stool, or hard, pellet-like stools.

Since you order ahead, I'd place the reorder when you have about a week of size 1 left, and make that order size 2.

good. i'm also trying to keep monthly spending under $5,200 while we're on leave pay, which comes in every two weeks and is about 70% of my salary, so i want to compare bulk pack prices. how do i do that without losing my mind

Compare by cost per diaper:

1. Take the pack price and divide by the count printed on the box.
2. Include shipping and any subscribe-and-save discount in the price.
3. Compare across pack sizes and brands in a simple sheet:

| Brand/pack | Price | Count | Cost per diaper |
|---|---|---|---|
| [brand A, box] | $ | | |
| [brand B, bulk] | $ | | |

Tips: the biggest packs aren't always cheapest, and a size can go unused if he outgrows it fast. With paychecks every two weeks, you could buy one bulk pack per pay period and set that amount aside in your monthly budget. A rough budget line is usually about 8-10 diapers a day at this age, so around 240-300 a month.
